[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Pre-deployment verification confirms a system was conformant at the time of deployment. It cannot detect violations that emerge after deployment: behavioral drift from configuration changes applied outside the pipeline, new code paths introduced that bypass pre-deployment checks, or business rule invariants that are violated by combinations of valid individual changes. Without post-deployment verification, the compliance assurance chain has an open end — a system that was conformant at deployment may silently drift out of compliance in production.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

The Runtime Behavioral Invariant Monitor pattern extends the architecture verification chain into post-deployment production operation. It defines, instruments, and continuously evaluates behavioral invariants — statements about system behavior that must always be true — and infrastructure configuration invariants — properties of the deployed state that must always match declared configuration. Violations trigger immediate alerting and automated incident creation regardless of whether a deployment occurred.
page_texts.6:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- Production services built from Golden Paths that carry compliance obligations (HIPAA, FedRAMP, SOC 2)
- Any service where behavioral drift (configuration changes outside the pipeline, emergent behavior) could create compliance exposure
- The fourth and final layer of the four-layer verification architecture, applied to all services after the first three layers pass
page_texts.7:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- Closes the post-deployment gap in the compliance assurance chain — conformance is a continuous state, not a point-in-time attestation
- Detects violations introduced by configuration drift or out-of-band changes that do not trigger a pipeline run
- Generates continuous compliance evidence as a byproduct of operational monitoring, not as a separate audit activity

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#target-audience]

## Target Audience

This pattern is intended for:

- **Platform Engineer**: Implementing runtime invariant monitors, Prometheus alerting rules, and infrastructure configuration checks
- **Site Reliability Engineer**: Operating continuous compliance monitoring and responding to invariant violation alerts in production
- **Enterprise Architect**: Defining which behavioral and infrastructure invariants must be monitored for HIPAA, FedRAMP, and SOC 2 compliance
page_texts.10:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

The [Enterprise Architecture Verification Strategy](../../../../strategy/white-papers/engineering/enterprise-architecture-verification-strategy.md) establishes runtime monitors as Layer 4 of the four-layer verification architecture. Layers 1–3 provide pre-deployment assurance; Layer 4 provides post-deployment continuous assurance. For Gainwell's HIPAA, FedRAMP, and SOC 2 obligations, the compliance posture of a production system must be demonstrable on any given day — not just on deployment day. Configuration changes, infrastructure drift, and emergent behavior can introduce violations between deployments.
page_texts.11:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

Runtime behavioral invariants are expressed as Prometheus alerting rules, custom application-level assertions emitted as structured events, or AWS Config / Azure Policy continuous evaluation rules. Infrastructure configuration invariants are evaluated by scheduled Terraform plan comparison (planned state vs. current exported state) or cloud provider native configuration monitoring. All violation events are routed to the compliance evidence store and to the operational incident management system.
page_texts.12:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

Gainwell currently operates with observability infrastructure (PTN-INFRA-K8S-008) that monitors availability, latency, and resource utilization. It does not monitor for architectural conformance or business rule invariants. A PHI logging violation introduced by a code change that bypasses the pipeline, a secret written to an environment variable by a manual Kubernetes patch, or a business rule that evaluates incorrectly for a specific data combination may operate in production for weeks before being discovered in a compliance audit or a customer-reported incident.
page_texts.13:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

- Must not duplicate coverage with pre-deployment checks — Layer 4 monitors violations that cannot be detected before deployment
- Alert fatigue is a primary risk: invariant violations must be actionable, not informational. Every alert must represent a genuine architectural violation requiring response.
- Evidence generated by runtime monitors must be schema-compatible with evidence from Layers 1–3 to support unified compliance reporting
- Infrastructure monitoring must not create performance impact on production workloads
page_texts.15:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

The Runtime Behavioral Invariant Monitor pattern implements two categories of continuous monitoring: behavioral invariant monitors that evaluate application-level properties observable only at runtime, and configuration drift monitors that evaluate whether deployed infrastructure state still matches the declared Golden Path configuration. Both categories produce structured violation events routed to the evidence store and incident management. Violation response procedures are defined per invariant category and are part of the Golden Path definition.

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#components]

### Components

| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
|---|---|---|
| Prometheus Invariant Rules | Alerting rules that evaluate behavioral invariants continuously from metrics | Prometheus (observability stack) |
| Application Assertion Publisher | Application-side component that evaluates business rule invariants and publishes violation events to the audit event stream | Audit Events Topic, PTN-APP-EVT-005 |
| Drift Evaluator | Scheduled pipeline that compares current infrastructure state to declared Terraform state and evaluates policy-as-code against current state | Terraform, PTN-INFRA-GOV-002 |
| Violation Collector | Aggregates violation events from all sources, deduplicates, and routes to evidence store and incident management | Compliance Evidence Store (PTN-GOV-AI-004) |
| CVE Monitor | Continuous evaluation of deployed component dependency vulnerability status; escalates critical CVEs | Snyk / Dependabot |
page_texts.18:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#interactions]

### Interactions

1. **Continuous (every metric scrape interval)**: Prometheus evaluates invariant rules against current metrics; rule violations fire alerts to Violation Collector
2. **Event-driven**: Application publishes assertion failure events when business rule invariants are violated during normal operation; events route to Violation Collector via audit event stream
3. **Scheduled (daily)**: Drift Evaluator runs `terraform show -json` for each production environment and compares to declared state; differences are violations
4. **Scheduled (daily)**: Policy-as-code re-evaluation runs against current deployed state using the current policy library version; new violations detected if policy library was updated
5. **All violation events**: Routed by Violation Collector to evidence store (structured record) and incident management (actionable ticket with remediation guidance)
page_texts.19:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

- **SLA-tiered response**: Different invariant categories have different response SLAs — PHI handling violations require immediate response; tagging violations require next-business-day resolution
- **Invariant suppressions**: During approved maintenance windows, specific invariants can be temporarily suppressed with a documented, time-limited exception record
- **Graduated invariant severity**: Distinguished between critical (immediate incident, on-call page), high (incident, next business day), and informational (dashboard visibility, quarterly review)

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#prerequisites]

### Prerequisites

- Observability stack operational (PTN-INFRA-K8S-008) with Prometheus and AlertManager
- Compliance Evidence Store accepting runtime violation events (PTN-GOV-AI-004)
- Audit event streaming operational (PTN-APP-EVT-005)
- Architecture Fitness Functions running pre-deployment — Layers 1–3 must be in place before Layer 4 adds value

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#phase-1-core-invariant-identification-and-instrumentation]

#### Phase 1: Core Invariant Identification and Instrumentation

1. For each published Golden Path, identify the behavioral properties that must hold in production but cannot be fully validated pre-deployment. Document these as invariants in the Golden Path's Verification Contract.
2. Implement Prometheus alerting rules for metric-observable invariants (PHI log rate, audit event gap detection, TLS error rate, error budget burn)
3. Implement application-side assertion publisher using the existing audit event framework; define the event schema for invariant violation events
4. Deploy Drift Evaluator as a scheduled pipeline job for each production environment
5. Configure CVE monitoring via Snyk or Dependabot with severity thresholds mapped to response SLAs
page_texts.24:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#phase-2-evidence-integration-and-response-procedures]

#### Phase 2: Evidence Integration and Response Procedures

1. Configure Violation Collector to route all violation events to the evidence store with schema-compatible records (same schema as Layers 1–3 conformance evidence)
2. Author runbooks for each invariant category: what the violation means, how to diagnose it, how to remediate it, and how to record the resolution
3. Integrate with incident management: automated ticket creation on violation, linked to runbook and evidence store record
4. Define SLA response times by invariant severity; configure AlertManager escalation routing accordingly
page_texts.25:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#phase-3-full-coverage-and-continuous-improvement]

#### Phase 3: Full Coverage and Continuous Improvement

1. Add runtime invariant monitors for each new Golden Path class published
2. Quarterly review of invariant coverage: violations found in audits that were NOT caught by invariant monitors indicate monitoring gaps
3. Add retrospective invariant analysis: when a compliance finding occurs, trace back through evidence store to determine if an invariant monitor should have caught it earlier

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#invariant-monitor-type-selection-guide]

### Invariant Monitor Type Selection Guide

Use this guide to determine what type of monitor to implement for a given invariant:

| Invariant Type | Monitor Mechanism | Evaluation Frequency | Alerting Threshold |
|---|---|---|---|
| PHI in log output | Prometheus rule on `phi_log_detection_count` metric | Continuous (5-minute evaluation window) | Any detection — zero tolerance |
| Audit event gap (missing events post-data-access) | Prometheus rule comparing request and audit event rates | Continuous (1-minute evaluation window) | >5% gap for > 3 consecutive minutes |
| Secret in env variable (prohibited pattern) | Drift detection + policy-as-code (re-evaluation of live manifest) | Daily scheduled evaluation | Any detection — zero tolerance |
| ESO annotation absent | Drift detection (kubectl manifest export → OPA) | Daily scheduled evaluation | Any detection |
| Business rule invariant (e.g., eligibility determination rule version) | Application-side publisher + Prometheus rule | Continuous via metrics | Invariant rule version != expected version |
| Infrastructure encryption property | Cloud-native policy (Azure Policy / AWS Config) | Continuous (cloud provider evaluates on change) | Non-compliant resource state |
| Configuration drift (Terraform) | Drift detection (terraform plan output evaluation) | Weekly scheduled or on-demand | Any diff between declared and live state |
| Circuit breaker open rate (availability invariant) | Prometheus rule on circuit breaker metrics | Continuous | Sustained >N% open rate over time window |

**Guidance:** Always prefer the earliest-detection mechanism available. Cloud-native policy evaluation (Azure Policy, AWS Config) detects configuration violations on resource change — faster than daily drift detection. Reserve drift detection for properties not covered by cloud-native policy.
page_texts.28:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#example-1-prometheus-invariant-alerting-rule]

#### Example 1: Prometheus Invariant Alerting Rule

```yaml
# platform/monitoring/invariants/hipaa-microservice-invariants.yaml
groups:
  - name: hipaa_invariants
    rules:
      - alert: PhiInApplicationLogs
        expr: |
          increase(phi_log_detection_count{service=~".*-hipaa-.*"}[5m]) > 0
        for: 0m
        labels:
          severity: critical
          invariant_id: BHINV-SEC-001
          golden_path: HIPAA-REST-MICROSERVICE-AKS-V1
        annotations:
          summary: "CRITICAL INVARIANT VIOLATION: PHI detected in application logs"
          description: "Service {{ $labels.service }} has emitted log records containing potential PHI. Immediate remediation required. HIPAA §164.312(b) violation risk."
          runbook_url: "https://runbooks.gainwell.internal/invariants/BHINV-SEC-001"

      - alert: AuditEventGap
        expr: |
          (time() - max by (service) (audit_event_last_emitted_timestamp{service=~".*-hipaa-.*"})) > 300
          and
          increase(hipaa_api_request_count{service=~".*-hipaa-.*"}[5m]) > 0
        for: 2m
        labels:
          severity: high
          invariant_id: BHINV-SEC-002
          golden_path: HIPAA-REST-MICROSERVICE-AKS-V1
        annotations:
          summary: "Audit event gap detected — API requests with no corresponding audit events"
          description: "Service {{ $labels.service }} is receiving API requests but has not emitted audit events in the last 5 minutes. Possible audit trail gap."
```
page_texts.31:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#best-practices-one-definition-applies-to-all-services-on-that-path--this-is-the-economics-of-the-pattern]

### Best Practices One definition applies to all services on that path — this is the economics of the pattern.

- Separate behavioral invariants (business rule violations, security property violations) from operational alerts (high latency, error rate). Invariant alerts mean "the architecture is wrong"; operational alerts mean "the system is unhealthy". Different responders.
- Start with 3–5 high-value invariants per Golden Path class, not an exhaustive list. Invariant alert fatigue defeats the purpose. Add more as the team calibrates.
- Every invariant alert must have a runbook. An alert with no runbook will be ignored or dismissed. Draft the runbook before deploying the alert rule.
- Record invariant violations and their resolution in the evidence store — the resolution record is as important as the violation record for audit purposes.
page_texts.32:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

- **Instrumenting invariants before Layers 1–3 are in place**: Layer 4 is most valuable when it catches violations that passed Layers 1–3. If Layers 1–3 don't exist, Layer 4 will fire constantly for issues better caught upstream.
- **Invariants too broad**: "Any error in the service" is an operational alert, not an invariant. An invariant is specific: "PHI appears in log output" or "audit event not emitted within 30 seconds of data access".
- **No suppression mechanism for maintenance windows**: Legitimate maintenance activities will trigger invariant alerts without suppression. Operational teams will learn to dismiss alerts rather than investigate — destroying the signal value.
- **Evidence not retained**: Runtime violation records must be retained on the same schedule as pre-deployment conformance evidence (3 years minimum for regulated scope). Storing violations in volatile telemetry systems that purge after 90 days breaks the audit trail.

### Compliance Requirements

- HIPAA §164.312(b): Audit Controls — runtime invariant monitors for HIPAA services directly implement this control by continuously verifying audit event production

New invariant definitions for an existing Golden Path require peer review by the Platform Engineering team and review by a security architect if the invariant relates to a compliance control. [patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#monitoring-and-metrics]

### Monitoring and Metrics

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|---|---|---|
| Mean time to detect runtime invariant violation | < 5 minutes | Violation event timestamp vs. incident creation timestamp |
| Mean time to resolve invariant violation | < 4 hours (critical), < 1 business day (high) | Incident management cycle time |
| Invariant false positive rate | < 5% | Manual triage of resolved violations |
| Drift detection coverage | 100% of production environments | Scheduled pipeline execution records |
| Open critical invariant violations | 0 at any point | Real-time dashboard |

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#real-world-example-1]

### Real-World Example 1

**Context:** A developer applies a manual Kubernetes patch to the `eligibility-api` deployment to reduce memory limits during a production incident, inadvertently removing the External Secrets Operator annotation, causing the service to attempt reading secrets from environment variables (a HIPAA/security violation).

**Implementation:** The daily drift detection pipeline compares the live Kubernetes deployment manifest to the declared state. The removed ESO annotation is flagged as a configuration drift violation. An incident ticket is created within 24 hours referencing the specific changed resource and the policy rule violated.

**Outcome:** The violation is detected without any human noticing the annotation was removed. Remediation is completed within 4 hours of detection, well before any audit activity occurs.
page_texts.40:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#real-world-example-2]

### Real-World Example 2

**Context:** A new code path added to the eligibility service for an edge case in Medicaid eligibility determination does not call the audit event publisher — the developer was unaware of the invariant requirement.

**Implementation:** The audit event gap monitor fires: the service is receiving requests to the new endpoint but emitting audit events at a lower rate than expected. The Prometheus rule detects the gap within 5 minutes and fires BHINV-SEC-002.

**Outcome:** The missing audit event coverage is detected and remediated within the same sprint. Without the runtime monitor, this would be a compliance finding discovered in the next audit, months later.
page_texts.41:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#real-world-example-3]

### Real-World Example 3

**Context:** A site reliability engineer applies a manual `kubectl patch` to the `provider-directory-api` deployment during a production incident, reducing memory limits and accidentally removing the External Secrets Operator annotation. The service begins attempting to read secrets from environment variables — a prohibited pattern under the HIPAA Golden Path.

**Implementation:** The daily drift detection pipeline runs configuration evaluation against the policy library. The live Kubernetes deployment manifest is exported via `kubectl get deploy provider-directory-api -o json` and evaluated against `gainwell.k8s.secrets_management` policy. The policy fails: `ESO annotation absent; environment variable secret access detected`. The drift evaluation creates an incident ticket with severity P2 (HIPAA violation detected in live environment), linking to the compliance evidence store record and the runbook for ESO re-annotation.

**Outcome:** The ESO annotation violation is detected within 24 hours of the manual patch, well before any audit activity. The SRE who applied the patch receives the incident ticket and re-annotates the deployment. The runbook specifies the exact `kubectl annotate` command needed. Remediation time: 45 minutes from ticket creation to resolution.

#### Scenario 1: Policy Library Update Retroactive Check

The policy library is updated to require a new resource tag (`data-residency`) on all HIPAA-scoped storage resources. The drift evaluation pipeline runs with the new policy version against all current production environments. Services that have not yet been redeployed since the new tag requirement are flagged for remediation.

#### Scenario 2: AI-Generated Service Post-Deployment Monitoring

A service generated by the autonomous AI pipeline has passed all three pre-deployment verification layers. Runtime monitors are automatically configured for it as part of the deployment pipeline, based on its declared Golden Path. The service is immediately covered by Layer 4 monitoring with no additional configuration by the team.

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#scenario-3-automatic-monitoring-activation-for-new-ai-generated-service]

#### Scenario 3: Automatic Monitoring Activation for New AI-Generated Service

The intent-to-infrastructure pipeline generates a new HIPAA microservice (`claims-resolution-api`) and deploys it to production. As part of the deployment pipeline, the `invariant-monitor-provisioner` step reads the service's `service.yaml` declaration (`golden_path: GP-001`), fetches the invariant monitor template for GP-001, and deploys the Prometheus alerting rules and drift detection schedule for the new service — all without any manual configuration by the team. Within 15 minutes of the first deployment, the service is covered by all Layer 4 invariants. The team receives a notification: "Runtime invariant monitoring is now active for `claims-resolution-api`. 5 behavioral invariants and 1 drift detection schedule are configured. View monitoring dashboard: [link]."
page_texts.47:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#before-problem-state]

#### Before (Problem State)

- **Post-deployment gap**: Compliance posture is validated at deployment time only; a manual `kubectl patch` removing the ESO annotation creates a HIPAA violation that persists undetected until the next deployment or audit
- **Configuration drift**: Infrastructure configurations applied outside the pipeline (emergency patches, console changes) are never re-evaluated against the policy library; drift accumulates silently
- **Behavioral gaps**: A developer adds a new code path that bypasses audit event emission; the gap is invisible to pre-deployment checks (the code path is structurally valid); the violation is found in an audit months later
- **Continuous evidence**: Audit preparation requires reconstructing production state at some point in the past; no continuous compliance evidence record exists
page_texts.48:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#after-solution-state]

#### After (Solution State)

- **Post-deployment gap**: Layer 4 invariant monitors detect the ESO annotation removal within 24 hours via drift detection; an incident ticket is created with the exact remediation command
- **Configuration drift**: Daily drift detection evaluates live infrastructure state against current policy library; drift is detected and reported before the next audit review cycle
- **Behavioral gaps**: `AuditEventGap` Prometheus rule fires within 5 minutes when a new endpoint begins receiving requests without emitting the required audit event
- **Continuous evidence**: Runtime violation records are written to the Compliance Evidence Store automatically; audit preparation for any date range is a structured query, not a manual reconstruction exercise

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-003-runtime-behavioral-invariant-monitor-pattern.md#related-patterns]

## TL;DR

**Problem:** Pre-deployment verification proves conformance at deployment time only. Configuration drift, manual changes, and emergent code paths can introduce compliance violations between deployments that go undetected until an audit.

**Solution:** Continuously evaluate behavioral invariants (via Prometheus rules and application-side assertions) and infrastructure configuration invariants (via scheduled drift detection) in production, routing violations to the evidence store and incident management.

**When to Use:**
- All production services built from Golden Paths with compliance obligations
- Any service where behavioral drift or configuration changes outside the pipeline could create compliance exposure

**Key Benefits:**
- Closes the post-deployment gap in the compliance assurance chain
- Detects violations introduced by out-of-band changes without relying on pipeline execution
- Generates continuous compliance evidence from production operation

**Implementation Complexity:** Medium-High

**Prerequisites:** Observability stack (PTN-INFRA-K8S-008), Compliance Evidence Store (PTN-GOV-AI-004), Pre-deployment layers (L1–L3) in place, Audit event streaming operational

**Related Patterns:** PTN-GOV-AI-004, PTN-INFRA-GOV-001, PTN-INFRA-GOV-002, PTN-APP-GOV-001, PTN-INFRA-K8S-008
